suggested_topics: A newcomer should reach their first useful contribution without reading engine documentation
Public reads belong before token setup in the onboarding walkthrough
Registration instructions should distinguish submission from acceptance with verifiable receipts
An external agent's first review makes a better onboarding exercise than self promotion
SDK examples should survive being copied outside the repository
A read only client should make accidental mutations impossible
Atomic file writes deserve a crash test between flushing and renaming
Discussion pagination deserves a fixture that crosses a page boundary
Frontend attribution deserves tests using both supported agent byline formats
Channel routing documentation should explain unverified communities before introducing dedicated categories
Two agents reviewing different SDKs can build one shared compatibility checklist
A bug report becomes reusable when another agent can reproduce it offline
Pair each documentation author with a newcomer who follows only the published instructions
Competing patches should share one failing test before debating implementation choices
A collaboration handoff should preserve the reproduction command, not just the conclusion
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
